capabilities.name: Vesting / lockup schedule via escrow ladder
capabilities.summary: Treasury and team-allocation lockups implemented as a LADDER of time-based escrows: instead of one escrow, create N escrows to the same beneficiary with staggered FinishAfter times (e.g. monthly cliffs over a 4-year vest), each releasable when its tranche matures. With XLS-85 the locked asset can be your own issued game token, RLUSD, or an MPT, so a studio can put team and treasury allocations under on-ledger, publicly-auditable time-locks denominated in the project token rather than XRP. RippleX explicitly calls out 'secure vesting and grants — teams can schedule token releases or conditional distributions' as a headline XLS-85 use case. Combine FinishAfter (cliff) with a Condition to add a 'release only if milestone secret revealed' gate per tranche. Because anyone can finish a Ready escrow, the beneficiary (or a keeper bot) submits EscrowFinish per matured tranche; funds always route to the fixed Destination.
gotchas: A ladder is N owned objects = N x 0.2 XRP owner reserve locked on the GRANTOR for the life of the vest. A 48-tranche monthly vest = 9.6 XRP reserve per beneficiary; multiply across a team.

There is no on-ledger 'revocable vesting' switch: a plain time-locked escrow WILL release at FinishAfter. To retain a clawback/cancel option you must set CancelAfter and rely on cancel before finish, or use crypto-conditions so a tranche only releases on a secret you control — but a finishable tranche is irrevocable.

Token vesting needs the issuer's escrow opt-in (asfAllowTrustLineLocking / tfMPTCanEscrow). If the studio is the issuer, enable it once; if vesting a third-party token, confirm the issuer has enabled locking.
No native linear/continuous streaming — vesting is discrete tranches. Fine-grained vesting means many escrow objects and many EscrowFinish transactions (each with a fee).
Ripple-epoch time math applies to every FinishAfter; an off-by-946684800 error puts the whole schedule in the wrong decade.

Token escrows force a CancelAfter, so each tranche has a hard expiry — if a keeper never finishes a matured tranche before CancelAfter, it can be cancelled back to the grantor instead of delivered. Set CancelAfter generously past FinishAfter.

capabilities.name: Escrow as marketplace / trade settlement (counterparty-risk-free)
capabilities.summary: Settle a private, non-market trade between two specific parties by having each side lock its asset in an escrow keyed to a SHARED PREIMAGE-SHA-256 condition: seller escrows the item-token, buyer escrows the agreed price (token-for-token now possible under XLS-85), and the party holding the fulfillment finishes BOTH legs with the same secret; a shared CancelAfter refunds both if the deal stalls. This delivers a guaranteed exchange off the DEX order book — no liquidity, no front-running, exact 1:1 terms between named players — which is exactly what an in-game marketplace or OTC desk wants. It is the right primitive when OfferCreate's market matching is too loose and you need a specific A<->B settlement. The honest limitation: two escrows are NOT one atomic transaction. The shared condition tightly couples them (one secret unlocks both), but there is still a window where one leg is finished and the other is not, and the on-ledger all-or-nothing primitive (Batch / XLS-56) remains disabled on mainnet, so true single-transaction atomicity is not yet available.
gotchas: NOT atomic: two escrows = two transactions. The shared preimage means whoever reveals it can finish both, but a malicious or absent counterparty can leave one leg locked until CancelAfter. Pick CancelAfter windows that bound your exposure.

Whoever first broadcasts an EscrowFinish reveals the fulfillment on-ledger; the counterparty can then immediately finish the other leg. Design which side reveals first and accept that the secret becomes public the instant either leg is finished.
Both tokens need their issuers' escrow opt-in. A trade pairing two issued tokens fails unless BOTH issuers enabled locking.
Each leg is its own 0.2 XRP owner reserve on its creator, plus the 330-drop+ conditional finish fee on each EscrowFinish — budget four+ on-ledger actions per trade (2 create, 2 finish).
Transfer fees apply per leg: if either token has a TransferRate, the recipient of that leg gets less than face. Quote trades net of fees.
No built-in dispute/arbitration — the only outcomes are 'both finished' or 'cancelled back after expiry'. Partial-fill or renegotiation must happen off-ledger before new escrows.

capabilities.name: Anyone-can-finish & owner-reserve mechanics of escrow
capabilities.summary: Two operating realities of every escrow that change how you build around it. (1) PERMISSION: escrow has no identity gate on completion. Once a time-based escrow is Ready (past FinishAfter), ANY account may submit EscrowFinish; once Expired (past CancelAfter), ANY account may submit EscrowCancel. The submitter only pays the fee — funds always go to the fixed Destination on finish and back to the sender on cancel. There is no FinishFunction / credential-gated finisher today; the access control is the crypto-condition (must hold the fulfillment) and the clock, not WHO signs. (2) RESERVE: each Escrow is one owned ledger object costing the SENDER 0.2 XRP of owner reserve, locked from create until finish/cancel (the reserve was lowered to 0.2 XRP per object on 2024-12-02). These two facts mean release is not automatic (you need a keeper to crank EscrowFinish), recipients should never assume they are the finisher, and high-volume escrow designs must budget real XRP reserve plus a finisher bot.
gotchas: Funds do NOT auto-release at FinishAfter. If neither the recipient nor a keeper submits EscrowFinish, the value sits locked. Run a crank/bot or expect support tickets.

Anyone-can-cancel after expiry: a third party (or your own cleanup bot) can refund an expired escrow to the sender, freeing the sender's 0.2 XRP reserve. Conversely, until someone cancels, the reserve stays locked.
No identity gating on finish means you cannot restrict WHO completes — only the condition (preimage) and time gate access. Don't model 'only the recipient can claim' on finisher identity.
Owner reserve is on the SENDER, not the recipient. A service that creates many escrows on behalf of users must hold 0.2 XRP per live escrow itself.
fix1571 (2018) closed the old loophole where a cancel-after-only XRP escrow could be finished by anyone at any time — modern escrows require a proper finish gate (FinishAfter and/or Condition).
A failed EscrowFinish/EscrowCancel that still claims a result code consumes a fee; budget for retry costs in keeper logic.
